wrong.why: Judah in מֶלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה denotes the kingdom Jehoshaphat ruled, not the patriarch represented by the slug judah.

missing.why: The verse calls David Jehoshaphat's father (דָּוִד אָבִיו) in the ancestral sense, while verse 41 identifies Asa as his father.

note: The remaining rows are supported, and the other explicit family statements already have equivalent recorded relationships.
